title: Handling fast questions and buying time

grammar.title: Fillers e strutture per guadagnare tempo (Let me think…, What I can tell you is…, echo questions)
grammar.explanation: Quando arriva una domanda veloce e inattesa, il vero problema non è la grammatica ma il silenzio. I madrelingua riempiono i primi secondi con formule fisse che danno tempo al cervello: 'That's a good question.', 'Let me think about that for a second.', 'How can I put this?'. La echo question ripete la parola chiave della domanda e intanto verifica il senso: 'The rollback plan? Sure.' oppure 'You mean for the production release?'. Poi rispondi con una struttura che delimita quello che sai: 'What I can tell you is that…', 'As far as I know…', 'Off the top of my head…'. Se non sai, non inventare: 'I'd rather not guess. Let me check and get back to you.' 'What I can tell you is (that) + frase' è una cleft sentence: il verbo centrale è 'is' (al passato 'was') e l'enfasi cade su ciò che segue. Evita di tradurre 'allora', 'cioè', 'diciamo': un filler inglese breve suona sicuro, una serie di 'so… so…' no.

examples.en: That's a good question. Let me think about that for a second.
The rollback plan? Sure, I can walk you through it.
What I can tell you is that no client data was affected.
examples.note: cleft sentence: delimita ciò che sai

examples.en: As far as I know, the custodian hasn't changed the format.
examples.note: segnala il limite della tua certezza

examples.en: Off the top of my head, it's around two hundred orders a day.
I'd rather not guess. Let me check and get back to you.

grammar.italianTrap: Sotto pressione gli italiani traducono 'allora…', 'diciamo che…', 'cioè…' con 'so…', 'let's say…', 'that is…' ripetuti in ogni frase, oppure dicono 'Good question, I think about it'. Meglio: 'Good question. Let me think about that for a second.' E per una stima a memoria: 'Off the top of my head, around fifty', non 'Let's say more or less fifty'.

phrases.en: Let me think about that for a second.
You mean for the production release?
phrases.it: Intendi per il rilascio in produzione?

phrases.en: What I can tell you is that the fix is already in staging.
phrases.it: Quello che posso dirti è che la fix è già in staging.

phrases.en: As far as I know, nothing has changed on their side.
phrases.it: Per quanto ne so, da loro non è cambiato nulla.

phrases.en: Off the top of my head, it's around fifty a day.
phrases.it: Così a memoria, sono circa cinquanta al giorno.

phrases.en: I don't have the exact figure in front of me, but it's roughly ten percent.
phrases.it: Non ho il dato preciso davanti, ma è circa il dieci per cento.

phrases.en: I'd rather not guess. Let me check and get back to you.
phrases.it: Preferisco non tirare a indovinare. Verifico e ti faccio sapere.

phrases.en: Can I come back to you on that by end of day?
phrases.it: Posso risponderti su questo entro fine giornata?

phrases.en: Bear with me a second, I'm just pulling up the dashboard.
phrases.it: Un attimo di pazienza, sto aprendo la dashboard.

phrases.en: The short answer is yes, but there's a catch.
phrases.it: In breve sì, ma c'è un però.

quiz.q: The bank's PM suddenly asks: 'How many failed orders did you have last month?' You don't know the exact number. Best start?
options: I don't know, sorry, it's not my area.
Let's say more or less, so, quite many.
Off the top of my head, around thirty. I'll confirm by email.
Last month? Is not my area.
quiz.why: 'Off the top of my head' segnala una stima a memoria, e la promessa di conferma ti protegge se il numero è sbagliato.

quiz.q: 'What I can tell you ___ that no client data was affected.'
options: are
is
it is
was being
quiz.why: Cleft sentence: 'What I can tell you is (that)…'. Il verbo centrale è 'is' (al passato 'was').

quiz.q: They ask: 'Is the rollback plan ready?' Which reply uses an echo question to buy time?
options: Yes or no?
Ready what?
What do you want to know exactly about it?
The rollback plan? Yes, let me walk you through it.
quiz.why: Ripetere la parola chiave ('The rollback plan?') ti dà un secondo per organizzare la risposta e conferma l'argomento.

quiz.q: You need ten seconds to find data on screen. What do you say?
options: Bear with me a second, I'm just pulling it up.
Wait.
Hold on, I search.
Please wait one moment because I am searching for it now on my screen.
quiz.why: 'Bear with me a second' + present continuous è il modo naturale e cortese di chiedere un attimo.

quiz.q: You don't want to guess the custodian's new cut-off time. What do you say?
options: I think it's probably four, or maybe five, or possibly even six.
I'd rather not guess. Let me check and get back to you.
I don't know, it's not my problem.
Guess five p.m.
quiz.why: 'I'd rather not guess' è onesto e professionale; tirare a indovinare crea false aspettative.

quiz.q: '___ I know, the vendor hasn't released the new version yet.'
options: As long as
As much as
As soon as
As far as
quiz.why: 'As far as I know' = per quanto ne so. Le altre hanno significati diversi (purché, tanto quanto, appena).

quiz.q: Which filler sounds most natural in English?
options: Cioè, the problem is the file.
Let's say that, so, the problem is the file.
Well, basically, the problem is the file.
That is to say, so, the file.
quiz.why: 'Well' e 'basically' sono filler brevi e naturali. 'Let's say' e 'that is to say' ripetuti come filler sono calchi di 'diciamo' e 'cioè'.

gapfill.text: That's a good question. Let me ___ about that for a second.
I don't have the exact figure in ___ of me, but it's around fifty.
___ I can tell you is that the fix is already in staging.

reorder.answer: What I can tell you is that nothing was lost.
Can I come back to you on that?

fluency.prompt: The partner bank's operations lead suddenly asks: 'How many transactions were unmatched last week?' You don't have the number. Buy time and give a safe answer. 30 seconds.
fluency.model: That's a good question. Off the top of my head, it was around forty, mostly small amounts. I'd rather not guess the exact figure, so let me check and get back to you by end of day.
keyPhrases: off the top of my head

fluency.prompt: The vendor's tech lead asks: 'Why didn't you use our new endpoint?' Use an echo question, then answer. 40 seconds.
fluency.model: The new endpoint? Sure. What I can tell you is that we tested it in March, but it didn't support bulk requests at the time. As far as I know, that's changed now, so we're happy to look at it again.
keyPhrases: what I can tell you is

fluency.prompt: Your CEO joins the call and asks: 'Can we go live with the new onboarding flow next week?' The answer is complicated. 45 seconds.
fluency.model: The short answer is yes, but there's a catch. How can I put this? The flow itself is ready, but the signature provider hasn't confirmed the production keys yet. If they confirm by Wednesday, we can go live on Monday.

fluency.prompt: The KYC provider asks for a figure you need to look up on screen. Buy a few seconds, then give it. 20 seconds.
fluency.model: Bear with me a second, I'm just pulling up the dashboard. OK, here it is: we ran about three thousand checks last month.
